title: One big array, no hierarchy

dataset.name: GHRSST MUR 0.01 degree global SST, daily 2002-2020, Zarr v2 on AWS (6443 x 17999 x 36000, chunks 5 x 1799 x 3600, 62 MB decoded each)

left.label: warp: rangefinder, windowed chunk reads at the view's resolution
left.note: Provisional permalink; record day and stretch.

right.label: cell: gridlook
right.note: Deliberately not iframed: gridlook would read the whole 36000 x 17999 field for one day (650 million cells, 100 chunks of 62 MB) before drawing. To see it try, open the pinned build with #https://mur-sst.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/zarr-v1 in its own tab. The DKRZ stores avoid this by publishing z-levels; MUR has no hierarchy.

gap: No spatial windowing in gridlook: level of detail comes from the data publisher, not the viewer. The warp side reads only the overview level and window the viewport needs.
bridge: Publish coarser siblings as a data product (MUR z-levels), generated by grout from the full array, so the cell side's existing hierarchy path works; and, in the other direction, add a viewport-windowed read to gridlook's regular-grid path.
todo: record the rangefinder permalink with a chosen day in left.url
stage the same day with 2x/4x/8x coarser sibling arrays on a CORS bucket (grout) to show gridlook drawing it once LOD is a data product; then right.url points at the coarsest sibling
